item.title: 'People are still afraid of those three letters': Fighting the stigma of HIV
item.description: That's a quote from former rugby star Gareth Thomas, who is HIV positive. At the International AIDS Conference in Rio this year, he spoke out about the isolation and discrimination tied to the virus.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: 'BRICS' forum brings together emerging economies, aimed at countering western dominance
item.description: India hosts the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging markets and developing countries.

item.title: Saudi Arabia forced to shut down crucial Red Sea pipeline after attacks
item.description: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.
item.content:encoded: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.

item.title: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries
item.description: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland

item.title: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
item.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: STR)

item.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
item.description: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.

item.description: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

item.title: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
item.description: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.
